note: SAMPLE CONTENT. Hand-written for this demo. Personas are fictional and only inspired by historical figures; no quotes are attributed to real people.
idea: Move a 20-person support team to a four-day week.

turns.text: Rested people solve harder tickets. Try it and the hiring pitch writes itself.
Customers call five days a week. Somebody has to answer on the fifth.
Look at the ticket data first: which hours actually carry the load?
If the metric is tickets closed, people will rush tickets to hit it in four days. Watch reopen rates.
Whatever the schedule, every person should get the same deal, not just the senior staff.
Stagger it: half the team takes Monday off, half takes Friday. Coverage stays at five days.
With staggering and a reopen-rate check, the risk is measurable.
Staggering keeps the meetings and loses the shared day off. I'd test a true four-day week on one pod too.

recommendation: Run a staggered four-day week for one quarter, with equal terms for everyone, tracking reopen rate and response time against last quarter.
dissent: The Inventor wants one pod to try a full shared day off as a comparison.
